EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by bands typical of a chloro-substituted benzylic alcohol.  Key matches are: (a) very strong bands at 715 cm⁻¹ and 539 cm⁻¹, characteristic of C–Cl stretching/bending vibrations and intensified by the presence of two chlorines; none of the bromine-free candidates can account for both positions, while a C–Br stretch would be expected lower (≈500 cm⁻¹) and would not give a second strong band near 715 cm⁻¹; (b) a strong C–O stretch of an aliphatic/benzylic alcohol at 1075 cm⁻¹; (c) an intense aromatic ring breathing mode at 831 cm⁻¹ plus ring C=C stretches at 1614 cm⁻¹ and 1458 cm⁻¹; (d) aromatic and aliphatic C–H stretches at 3081, 3031, 2947 and 2854 cm⁻¹, consistent with a benzyl –CH₂–OH group.  The spectrum shows no clear N–H (≈3300 cm⁻¹) or strong C=O (∼1650–1750 cm⁻¹) fundamentals, disfavoring the amide- or carbonyl-containing candidates (6, 7, 10).  Overall, only candidate 1 (OCc1cc(Cl)ccc1Cl, 2,4-dichlorobenzyl alcohol) simultaneously provides the required two C–Cl bonds, a benzylic alcohol C–O, and an aromatic ring, fitting the major Raman features.
